items.titleEn: Intel stock plunges 17% after weak Q4 forecast overshadows AI growth
items.summaryEn: Buy AMD. If Intel’s PC and production issues persist, OEMs and PC supply chains keep shifting share toward competitors. AMD is the cleanest beneficiary of Intel’s client-computing stumble while the broader AI/data-center buildout continues. The setup is simple: Intel’s guidance shock signals share pressure in PCs, and AMD’s platform momentum should translate into higher unit demand and better mix. Key Risk: PC demand doesn’t just slow—it collapses across the whole market, hurting AMD’s volumes and forcing margin compression. Sell INTC. The stock got a big earnings beat, but the market is punishing the forward view: Q4 revenue $15–$16B vs $17.3B expected and EPS 25c vs 45c. The thesis is that PC weakness is worsening faster than Intel modeled (memory-price impact “sooner and deeper”), and the Israel facility disruption adds real near-term supply risk. AI/data-center growth can’t offset a client-computing slowdown when guidance is the problem.

items.titleEn: Oracle stock falls 4%: why experts aren't bothered
items.summaryEn: Buy Oracle (ORCL). The news is a clear step-up in free-cash-flow timing: positive FCF expected in 2H FY2028 (~12 months earlier), with capex peaking in FY2027–28 then stepping down in FY2029. That improves the odds Oracle funds AI infrastructure internally instead of repeatedly tapping capital markets. Add the higher pricing on 5-year contracts (~$16B per GW vs ~$10B) and management’s ~28% return on invested capital—this supports margin durability through the ramp. Key Risk: AI infrastructure delivery slips (power/permitting/labor), delaying the ~10GW ramp and pushing FCF positivity back out. Buy data-center power/utility exposure tied to new AI capacity buildouts: NextEra Energy (NEE). Oracle’s plan to add ~10GW of AI infrastructure capacity by FY2028 implies sustained demand for power generation and grid upgrades. Second-order effect: even if Oracle’s sites face timing risk, the power build and interconnection work tends to be longer-cycle and less reversible, supporting utility earnings visibility.

items.titleEn: Palantir stock falls, why are analysts bullish on the stock
items.summaryEn: Buy Palantir (PLTR). The setup is accelerating AI ROI: analysts expect a Q3 revenue beat and continued growth into 2027, with JPMorgan specifically arguing the market is shifting from AI experiments to measurable returns—where Palantir already shows profitability and cash flow. The catalyst is the Nov 2 earnings window plus “positive catalyst watch.” Key Risk: Q3 results disappoint (revenue growth or margins) and investors decide the ROI story is hype, forcing a valuation reset. Sell the S&P 500 (SPY) relative to Palantir (PLTR): go long PLTR, short SPY. The thesis is that Palantir’s premium valuation can hold only if growth/profitability keep beating; analysts are lining up for that outcome ahead of earnings. If the market keeps rewarding “AI that produces returns,” PLTR should outperform broad equities.

items.titleEn: DoorDash offers $17 billion for Instacart in what would be a big consolidation for grocery delivery
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: DoorDash is offering $17 billion to buy Instacart in a deal that could consolidate the grocery delivery business in the U.S. and abroad. Instacart, founded in 2012, specializes in grocery and convenience store delivery in the U.S. and Canada. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app would remain, and Instacart's 600,000 shoppers—who are independent contractors—would be able to continue fulfilling orders as before.

items.titleEn: Microsoft stock falls as $25B bond plan draws focus despite Azure growth
items.summaryEn: Buy Microsoft (MSFT). Earnings beat and Azure growth (48% vs 44.3% forecast) confirm AI demand. The capex miss is timing (third‑party capacity delivery delays), not a cut to AI investment plans; management guides capex back above $50B next quarter and acceleration in the second half of FY27. The $25B bond plan is a financing choice, not a demand collapse, and free cash flow still beat expectations. Key Risk: Azure growth slows materially because customers pull back on AI infrastructure spending, not just because of delivery timing. Sell Nvidia (NVDA) or reduce exposure. The market is fixated on Microsoft’s lower-than-expected capex and free cash flow, which can pressure near-term AI hardware sentiment even if Microsoft says it’s delivery timing. That creates a window where AI infrastructure names trade down on “spending concern” headlines before the delayed capacity actually ramps.
